alternatives.root_cause: Checkout holds a wrong shipping address or port in its configuration.
alternatives.why_not: Checkout's change window was observed and held nothing, and the failure coincides instead with an image change recorded on shipping.

alternatives.root_cause: Shipping is cut off from the network so callers cannot reach it.
alternatives.why_not: Callers fail fast at connect time rather than hanging to deadlines, and shipping's log shows repeated process starts rather than complaints about unreachable peers.

alternatives.root_cause: Shipping's process is frozen while its socket still accepts.
alternatives.why_not: A frozen process writes nothing; shipping is writing startup output repeatedly and callers get immediate connection failures.

verdict.summary: Shipping's image reference was repointed to a wrong artifact (an ad-service build) at 14:36, so the shipping container crash-loops on startup and never serves, leaving callers unable to resolve or reach it.
verdict.reasoning: Checkout alerted first but its own error ratio did not depart from baseline (tr_a6fc3459f2f0) and no change was made to it (tr_de541bf0a9f7); every failing checkout trace fails on the single hop out to shipping with a name-resolution/connection failure, while all its other dependencies (cart, currency, product-catalog) answer in sub-millisecond time (tr_589438b5ff79). The change log for shipping shows repeated repointing of its image reference to an artifact tagged for a different service, the last at 14:36, minutes before the 14:40 onset (tr_916583aacdfd). Shipping's own log shows only repeated JVM/agent startup banners recurring every few seconds with no steady-state service output, the signature of a container restarting continuously rather than a frozen, partitioned or disk-full process (tr_c519571eebc8). The downstream alerting set (accounting, email, payment, quote, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy) follows from failed order placement propagating toward callers.
open_questions: Whether the endpoint is unreachable because the pod never becomes ready or because its DNS record was withdrawn was not directly observed.
The elided middle of the shipping log may contain an explicit startup error naming the mismatched artifact; it was not retrieved.
Whether the earlier image flips at 13:52 and 14:16 caused shorter, unalerted outages was not checked.
